insight: For Ghana, hydration breaks in the 2026 World Cup have generally been a positive turning point, with the team gaining momentum in 6 out of 8 breaks, indicating a slight increase in performance after the pause. The numbers suggest that when Ghana is not pressing before a break, they tend to come out stronger, with an average increase in momentum of 0.083 minutes, which can be crucial in close matches. However, when they are pressing before a break, the opposite is true, with a significant drop in momentum, averaging a loss of 0.300 minutes, and they have been unable to regain their footing after the break in these instances. Overall, Ghana seems to benefit from the brief respite, allowing them to regroup and refocus, unless they are already exerting high pressure, in which case the break appears to disrupt their rhythm.
